corrections.what: Both harnesses refuse a return code outside {0, 1}, and every batch now carries two sentinels: one that must succeed and one that must fail with a known diagnostic.
why: The eligibility probe reads acceptance from the ABSENCE of a diagnostic. That makes two silent failures indistinguishable from a clean run: a frontend that died halfway through, and a frontend that stopped reporting. The first is caught by the return code; the second is caught by a sentinel that MUST produce a diagnostic - if its known error is missing, the batch refuses.

The passing sentinel catches the third: a file that did not elaborate to its end, because the preamble failed or a parse error swallowed the tail. Everything above such a point is an answer to a file we did not write.
This is the maxErrors bug generalised. That one cost 663 statements of false eligibility and was caught by a single substring; these are the other doors into the same room.

corrections.what: `#ser` now answers FVERR when the elaborated term still carries a metavariable or contains `sorryAx`.
why: `ser` maps EVERY `.mvar` to the constant string `(mv)`. Two different propositions that both end in an unassigned metavariable therefore serialize to the same string and digest identically - `(1 2 3)` and `(4 5 6 7)` are the reviewer's pair and they collided. A witness that says two different things are the same is worse than no witness.

`sorryAx` is the same failure by the other door. `withoutErrToSorry` stops `elabTerm` from turning its OWN errors into a sorry, but a term whose source contains `sorry` still elaborates cleanly to one, and every such term shares the same skeleton.

Both now refuse. Measured after the change: all 2,319 eligible statements still serialize, so the guard costs nothing on the covered set and closes a collision that would have been invisible in B1's rate.

corrections.finding: review C2, implemented as `unaccounted diagnostics refuse` rather than `any diagnostic refuses` - A DEVIATION, stated
corrections.what: A batch refuses when the return code is outside {0, 1}, or when an `error:` line belongs to no `#ser` command, or when it belongs to a command whose tag reported SUCCESS.
why: The review asked for a two-line guard refusing on `returncode != 0 or ': error' in output`, and that guard was safe against the serializer as it stood. H2 changed what it is safe against: since `#ser` now rejects a residual metavariable, a term like `(1 2 3)` produces a frontend error line AND a correctly-reported FVERR for its tag. Under the blunt rule, one pathological statement would abort an entire registered run.

B2 reserves aborting for REFUSALS, not FAILURES: 'FAIL - the surface elaborated with errors - counts against B1. REFUSED - the toolchain is absent or an input escapes containment - aborts the run.' A statement that fails to elaborate is a data point. A batch whose diagnostics do not add up is not.

So the guard is stated over TAGS instead of over the whole output, which is strictly stronger where it matters: it catches an error in the PREAMBLE (which the blunt rule would also catch) and an error on a command that claimed success (which the blunt rule catches only by refusing everything). Attribution is exact because exactly one `#ser` command is emitted per line.

An error on a command that produced NO line is deliberately allowed through: that is a parse error, the one failure no elaborator can catch, and `_run_with_reprobe` owns it - re-probing the tag alone before calling it a failure.

corrections.artifact: scripts/foreign_voice_lexicon.py, and a note that data/foreign_voice/lexicon.json was DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED

why: L1: F4 cannot fail given F2 and F3, and a gate list whose entries are only implied by other entries is a gate list a reader has to derive. The note says so at the line, and says that if F2 or F3 is ever weakened this stops being redundant.

L7, and the reason it is here rather than in the table: `coverage.constructive_check` says the coercion arrow appears as '7 runs across 4 statements' while the refusal row says '9 occurrences across 4 statements'. Both are true and the units differ - 9 arrow CHARACTERS form 7 maximal operator RUNS, because two statements carry adjacent arrows. Reading them as contradictory is the natural reading and it is wrong.

THE TABLE WAS NOT EDITED TO FIX IT, and that is now a standing rule rather than a one-off: `data/foreign_voice/lexicon.json`'s digest is the seed of B0d's draw, so any change to it re-draws the hundred and un-seals a hundred hand-authored sentences. corrections.artifact: docs/DESIGN-foreign-voice.md path names vs the tree
corrections.what: The design's §3.1 names `data/foreign/loanword_lexicon.json` and `scripts/foreign_voice.py`; §3.3 names `experiments/foreign_register.json`. The tree uses `data/foreign_voice/lexicon.json`, `data/foreign_voice/register.json` and (in phase 2) `scripts/foreign_voice.py`.
why: The lexicon sits beside its interpretation, its preview, its selection rule, its sealed renderings and its register in one directory, mirroring `data/realization/`. A `data/foreign/` holding one file and `experiments/` holding another would scatter six artifacts that are read together and digested together.

The register lives in `data/` rather than `experiments/` because it is INPUT to the run, not output of one: B4 makes freezing it a precondition of rendering. `experiments/` in this repository holds what a run produced - `realization_rate.json`, `realization_census.json` - and `experiments/foreign_voice_rate.json` will land there when the run happens.

Recorded rather than left for a reader to reconcile, because the design is the preregistration record and a path in it that does not exist is exactly the kind of drift this project reads as a warning.

corrections.what: The numeral-literal regex no longer matches a digit run inside an identifier.
why: `x_2`, `a1` and `v0` carry digit runs the numeral pair is never asked to spell. Harmless today - `2` is in the registered domain - and not harmless in principle: a slot spelled `v1000000000000000000` would have been filed as an out-of-domain literal and the statement registered as unrenderable for a reason that is not true of it.

corrections.what: The `_run_with_reprobe` guard that refused a batch in which EVERY tag failed to answer is removed. The batch sentinels are the sole authority on file-level failure.
why: The guard read 'all tags missing' as 'the file broke'. C-V1 is the one control built to feed the oracle deliberate nonsense - statements inverted through a SCRAMBLED table - and a batch of that can legitimately have every tag fail to parse. The guard turned the control into a run abort, which is B2 backwards: a garbage input is a data point, a broken harness is a refusal.

The sentinels subsume it and are strictly better. They sit AFTER every statement, so a preamble that did not compile, or a parse error that swallowed the file to EOF, leaves them unanswered and the batch refuses. If they answered, the file was fine and the missing tags are genuine parse errors however many there are - which is exactly the distinction the removed guard could not draw.

Found by a smoke test of the run's own code paths on fifteen statements, BEFORE the registered run produced any number. The first attempt at the registered run was stopped for unrelated instrumentation gaps and had written nothing when it was stopped; no gate reading existed at any point during this fix.

corrections.what: C-V1 gains a four-way failure-mode split and a contrast computed on the SAME statement set; the artifact gains a `verdicts` block adjudicating every gate and control against the design's own §6/§7 sentence.
why: C-V1's voiding sentence has three clauses and the third - 'if both are near zero, the gate is untested and the reading is void' - cannot be adjudicated from a rate alone. A skeleton rate of zero means the control worked if the misses are `elaborated_to_a_different_digest`, and means the gate never ran if they are `scrambled_failed_to_elaborate`. The runner recorded only the rate, so the control would have been unreadable in exactly the case §7 legislates for.
The contrast is now against the true renderer's rate ON THE SAME STATEMENTS, because §7 says so and because a ratio between two different denominators is not a ratio.

The verdicts block exists so the adjudication lives in the artifact rather than in whoever writes the release. A run that reports numbers and leaves FIRES/MISSES/VOID to prose is a run whose verdict can drift from its data. It also encodes the precedence: a VOID control outranks a cleared B1 floor, because a voided control voids the reading it gates.
Both gaps were found by reading the reporting requirements against the runner, before any number existed. The first attempt at the run was stopped with an empty log and no artifact.

c_v4.control: C-V4 - the near-miss null, and the control this design did not have
c_v4.registered_before: any run of scripts/measure_foreign_voice.py, and before scripts/foreign_voice.py existed in the tree
what_it_measures: B1 compares digests of ELABORATED TERMS, so any rendering error that elaboration erases, or that rule R silently regenerates, is invisible to it. C-V4 measures how large that blind spot is.

The design states the bound as part of the claim rather than as a caveat: identity holds 'up to what elaboration erases and what the preamble rule regenerates; a rendering error confined to either is invisible to B1; C-V4 bounds how often that is the case.'
procedure: For each mutation class below, draw a sample from the COVERED set by the committed seeded rule; apply exactly ONE mechanical mutation to the RENDERED ENGLISH; invert; elaborate; compare the digest against the unmutated round trip's digest.
The mutation is applied to the English, never to R(s) and never to the inverse output, because the question is whether the SENTENCE determines the term.
an_fverr_counts_as_the_digest_differing: A mutation that breaks elaboration IS DETECTED. If the mutated sentence inverts to something the pinned binary refuses, the gate has distinguished the mutant from the original just as decisively as a differing digest would, and counting it as 'no difference' would score the control against itself.
So for every threshold below, `differs` = (the digest differs) OR (the mutant produced FVERR).

The artifact reports the two sub-counts separately anyway, because a class whose detections are ALL elaboration failures is a class where the gate is reading Lean's grammar rather than the rendering, and a reader is owed that distinction even though it does not change the pass or fail.
sample_rule: pool = the covered set, sorted by statement id;
for each mutation class, keep only statements that ADMIT the mutation - a preamble with at least two binders for swap_binder, at least one grouping pair for drop_group, and so on;
seed = int(sha256_lf(data/foreign_voice/lexicon.json)[:16], 16), the same seed B0d's draw uses, so no sample in this cycle is a knob;
random.Random(seed).shuffle(pool); take the first `sample_size`; report the admitting denominator beside the sample size.

mutations.name: drop_ascription
mutations.what: delete the `of type <typeword>` phrase from the preamble

mutations.name: swap_binder
mutations.what: exchange two `variable <numeral>` tokens IN THE PREAMBLE PHRASE ONLY, leaving their occurrences in the body alone

mutations.name: drop_group
mutations.what: delete one matched `the quantity` / `end quantity` pair

mutations.name: shift_group
mutations.what: move one `end quantity` one token later, reassociating a single operator

mutations.name: drop_binder
mutations.what: delete one `variable <numeral>` token from the preamble binder list

per_class_thresholds_replace_the_pooled_: The design's section 7 sets one pooled floor: 'If fewer than 95% of mutations change the digest, B1 is measuring the preamble rule and not the rendering, and the reading is void.'

A pooled floor over a mix that includes a mutation which is blind BY CONSTRUCTION does not measure what it says it measures - it measures the mix. Four blind drop_binders out of a hundred would eat the whole 5% budget without telling anyone anything, and a thousand of them would void a reading that is fine.

So the pooled floor is replaced, before any run, by FOUR per-class floors at 0.90 each, and the fifth mutation is excluded from the voiding pool and reported as a measurement in its own right. Any one of the four classes falling below 0.90 voids the C-V4 reading and, through it, the sentence B1 is allowed to make.
Replacing a floor is a preregistration act, and this is it: dated, in a file whose digest predates the run and predates the renderer.

drop_binder_is_blind_by_construction.claim: The preamble rule REGENERATES what this mutation deletes. Rule R collects the free identifiers of the body and prepends a binder for each, so deleting a binder from the preamble phrase leaves the round trip's R(s) identical to the original's in almost every case, and B1 cannot see the deletion.
drop_binder_is_blind_by_construction.why_it_is_not_a_bug_in_the_control: It is the concrete, countable form of the section 8 non-claim. 'Up to what the preamble rule regenerates' is an abstraction until a number is put under it. This is the number.

expectation_carried_from_the_review_audi.the_one_that_moved: a binder whose type was Int rather than Rat - deleting it let the preamble rule rebind that identifier at Rat, which IS a different term
expectation_carried_from_the_review_audi.measured_by: the fresh-eyes review's independent inverse audit, not by this repository's renderer
expectation_carried_from_the_review_audi.why_it_is_an_expectation_and_not_a_resul: Preregistering a threshold from a number this cycle's own instrument produced would be setting the bar where the arrow landed. The registered run RE-MEASURES this with scripts/foreign_voice.py, and a divergence from 1-of-24 is itself a reportable finding rather than a discrepancy to reconcile.

what_the_run_must_report: the fraction of drop_binder mutations that moved the digest, with its denominator;
for each one that moved, WHY - the review's single mover was a type change, and a mover with a different cause is a different fact;
the sentence naming this as the measured boundary of what B1 cannot see, in the same artifact as B1's rate.

correction_to_the_designs_s7_prediction.design_says: section 7, C-V4: 'The binder-swap mutation is expected to be the one that most often fails to move the digest, precisely because rule R regenerates the preamble from the inverse output.'
correction_to_the_designs_s7_prediction.measured: 16 of 16 binder-swap mutations MOVED the digest
why_the_prediction_was_wrong: Rule R regenerates the preamble by collecting the free identifiers of the BODY and SORTING them. The design read 'regenerates' as 'restores whatever the preamble said', which would indeed hide a swap.

But a sorted regeneration cannot reproduce an unsorted swap. The mutation leaves the body alone, so the inverse hands back a binder list in swapped order while the body's occurrences are unchanged; the identifiers therefore bind in a different order than the original, which is a genuinely different forallE nesting. The serializer reports it faithfully because de Bruijn indices carry binding structure and the names are already gone.
So the very property the design expected to cause blindness - the preamble being regenerated by rule - is what makes the swap visible.

drop_binder is blind for the reason section 7 attributed to swap_binder, and the two are not interchangeable. The design's sentence is corrected here rather than in the design, because the design is the preregistration record and this file is where its dated corrections live.

rule: EVERY sentence that quotes B1 states the covered set's composition in the same sentence. The design fixes two of the three parts - 'n of N, of which X% is lean_workbook.ground.v1' - and this block adds the third, which the review found missing.

THE THIRD PART: the number of DISTINCT elaborated-term digests in the covered set, beside the number of statements. B1 is a rate over digest identities, and a covered set whose statements do not have distinct terms is a covered set whose rate is over fewer independent things than its denominator suggests.
The run artifact carries all three and the release sentence quotes all three. A B1 rate published with n and without the distinct-digest count is a rate that overstates its own resolution.

measured_2026_08_24.measured_by: scripts/foreign_voice_oracle.py over R(s) for the eligible set, before any rendering existed
measured_2026_08_24.reproduces: the fresh-eyes review's independent audit measured 2,180 distinct over 2,319 with 116 collision classes; this repository's own instrument reproduces both figures exactly
measured_2026_08_24.what_a_collision_is: Two corpus statements whose R(s) elaborate to the SAME term - `∀ a b : Rat, a^2 + b^2 ≥ 2*a*b` and `∀ x y : Rat, x^2 + y^2 ≥ 2*x*y` are two statement ids and one theorem, and the serializer is binder-name-independent by construction, so it says so. That is the serializer working, not failing.
measured_2026_08_24.why_it_must_be_quoted: 94.0% of the covered set is a statement with a term of its own; the other 6.0% shares. A reader told '2,313 statements' and not told '2,176 distinct terms' will read the rate as covering 2,313 independent facts. It does not, and the difference is the kind of thing this project retracts later if it is not said first.
